transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, my regular doctor actually sent me here. 

Apparently my weight has dropped pretty low, and... well, everyone is making a big fuss about it. But honestly, I feel like being this light just helps me keep up with my work in the shop. It keeps me from getting slowed down, you know?
When you look in the mirror, how do you feel about the way your body looks right now?

I'm not really sure. I don't spend a lot of time staring in the mirror, to be honest. When I do, I just see... myself. I look fine. I certainly don't see whatever it is my doctor or everyone else is seeing. I just look normal to me.
Do you ever hear voices or see things that other people don't seem to notice?
No, nothing like that. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. My mind is perfectly clear.
Could you describe what your typical daily food intake looks like?

Well, it's pretty simple. On workshop days, I usually just have tea... and maybe a few careful bites of something. Stopping to sit down for a real meal just feels unnecessary to me. It kind of throws off the rhythm and the control I've got over the day, you know? So I just keep it very light and keep working.
Do you engage in any specific activities, such as intense exercise or other methods, to make sure you don't gain weight?

No, I don't do anything like that. I mean, my work is pretty physical—being a carpenter keeps me moving and on my feet all day. So I don't really see a need to go to a gym or run miles or anything. And I don't use any... other methods to keep my weight down, either. Just keeping my eating light is enough.
Are you afraid that if you were to eat more or gain weight, it would have a negative impact on your ability to work or your sense of control?

Yes, I do worry about that. If I eat anything heavy... or even let myself have the kinds of foods we used to make for the holidays, I start worrying right away. I just immediately think I'm going to gain weight, and that I'll lose the grip I've worked so hard to keep. So it really does feel like I'd lose that sense of control if I changed how I eat.
